policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'from the daughter of Zion' is compatible both with the qere's prefixed preposition in מִבַּת and the ketiv's separately written מן בת; the alternative_rendering note concerns 'majesty'/'beauty' and does not decide this unit.
ASV 'their pleasant things' does not distinguish the qere מַחֲמַדֵּיהֶם from the ketiv מחמודיהם; both candidate readings remain compatible, and no mapped textual note decides between them.

ASV's vocative 'all ye peoples' does not uniquely distinguish the qere הָעַמִּים from the anarthrous ketiv עמים; the English address remains compatible with either, and no mapped textual note decides the unit.
